name: audio deepfake detection evaluation
description: Current text-to-speech algorithms produce realistic fakes of human voices, making deepfake detection a much-needed area of research. While researchers have presented various techniques for detecting audio spoofs, it is often unclear exactly why these architectures are successful: Preprocessing steps, hyperparameter settings, and the degree of fine-tuning are not consistent across related work. Which factors contribute to success, and which are accidental? In this work, we address this problem: We systematize audio spoofing detection by re-implementing and uniformly evaluating architectures from related work. We identify overarching features for successful audio deepfake detection, such as using cqtspec or logspec features instead of melspec features, which improves performance by 37% EER on average, all other factors constant. reputation: A useful benchmark in audio spoofing/deepfake detection research, especially for comparing feature representations and generalization.
notes: Non-LLM audio benchmark; results are highly sensitive to feature extraction, training setup, and dataset shift. Generalization is a major concern.
